title: Every candidate-typed scorer registers a name-neutrality proof, or says why not
deviations_from_card: Registered 38 of 41 discovered functions (card minimum was 12-14); only the 3 name-addressing letter drafters (draft_outreach/rejection/offer) are EXEMPT. Carriers redact the name inside the declared paths instead of popping whole keys, so ranking order stays compared (fairness_check 'ranking' is a list of labels). PERTURBATIONS also adds the 'Candidate' fallback label and the titled Ing. pair (union, never smaller). Prose perturbations compare feminine vs masculine line of the pair, since prose vs no prose adds an evidence item. The -ová mutation vs the three older suites was MEASURED once (scratch script: test_fairness 16/16, test_name_neutrality 10/10, test_recruiter 7/7 green under the patch) and recorded in the commit body and test docstring; the permanent test pins only that the registry catches it. Code landed as a single test(...) commit with the three suite switches (a test-only commit would have been red on the three-suites case), then a docs commit.
notes: Red-before: with neutrality.py absent, the test module failed at import (all 26 cases red). Acceptance 8/8. The registry runs in about 2s. test:python:gate: 2981 tests OK, skipped=4 (baseline 5 not raised); the first run had one unrelated Windows timer flake (test_logger StageTimer 14ms<15ms), which passed alone and on the full re-run. test:eval:ci 0, and the gender probe now reports 4 pairs (was 3). test:unit 10395/10395. test:perf exit 1 on ONE line: app/api/tasks/route.ts 3090 KB vs ceiling 3088 KB. I touched no TS (only pipeline/jobfit/*.py and 2 docs), so this overage comes from a sibling's uncommitted app/ files. No typecheck needed: codegen does not read eval/ or tests/. The docs commit landed under the lock, which I then released. The full test:unit ran on the code commit while the docs were being edited (docs do not feed unit tests).
